hypothesis: Question: is the remaining development error of the HGB leader dominated by estimator variance/capacity (fixable by bagging or a slower, more regularized boosting schedule) or by period-level shift (not fixable without level extrapolation)? Contrasting expectations: (A) variance/capacity dominates -> a date-bootstrap bag of 6 HGBs or a 600-iteration lr=0.04 min_samples_leaf=40 HGB lowers development RMSE by roughly 1-4% versus 59.98; (B) transfer/level shift dominates -> all branches stay within about 1% of the leader and forward-fold RMSE remains far above development RMSE, confirming that interpolation-style variance reduction does not address the transfer gap. How prior evidence changed my view: idea-ae78bf showed loss/target transforms are not the lever (59.976 vs baseline HGB 59.993, essentially identical), and idea-fa3d93 showed that aggressive YoY level scaling selected by forward folds (yoy_ratio 2.09, blend chosen, forward fold RMSE 71 vs base 117) badly hurt development RMSE (99.8 vs 60), so within-training forward folds overstate the level gap that the final model (which sees Jan-Apr 2012) actually faces. I therefore stop pursuing level extrapolation and run the conservative check; bootstrap by whole dates respects within-date dependence. Selection uses the same two 61-day forward holdouts as idea-ae78bf so the selection protocol is held fixed; only the candidate set changes. Unverified exploratory rationale; if worse than the leader the default lowest-development-RMSE selection still applies.
